text:
Alicia (platform): Heads-up — putting together the reranking endpoint spec. Need quick sync on scoring semantics + sensible caps before I send to API reviewers.
Ben (api): Nice. main things we need: 1) what the "score" number represents (probability vs raw logit), 2) ordering direction (higher=better?), 3) max candidates allowed per request, 4) whether we return rank and score, 5) telemetry tags we attach.
Priya (eng-ml): From model side: raw model output is typically a logit-like score. For downstream consumers it's nicer to have a normalized 0..1 score. But normalization depends on model and dataset — can be misleading.
Ben (api): So do we return both? e.g. "score" (float, normalized 0-1) and "raw_score" optional flag?
Priya (eng-ml): I like that. Default: only normalized score 0..1 labeled "score". Add query param include_raw_scores=true to include "raw_score" (may be uncalibrated).
Marco (console): If we expose both, console dashboards must pick one canonical metric for histograms. We should probably use "score" (normalized) for UI charts. Also tag the model_version so dashboards can compare.
Zoe (product): UX question — what about tie-breaking? Consumers expect deterministic ordering.
Alicia (platform): We should document deterministic stable-sort: sort by score desc, then by candidate_id asc. Also expose "rank" (1-based) so clients don't need to re-sort.
Ben (api): Limits: proposal — default max_candidates=100, max hard cap 1000. We enforce hard cap server-side to avoid O(N log N) blowups on large candidate lists. Thoughts?
Priya (eng-ml): 100 default seems reasonable for most rerankers. But some enterprise customers feed 500-1000 candidate sets. 1k cap is fine if we gate compute and warn in telemetry.
Marco (console): Tie to quotas and dashboards: we should surface candidate_count per request in cost breakdown and add a per-request field tokens_estimated (rough). Also add a per-model latency p95 by candidate_count bucket.
Ben (api): Agree. Also add parameter rerank_mode: ["score_desc","rank_only"]. But maybe overkill. Simpler: an argument sort_by=["score","custom_field"]?
Priya (eng-ml): Keep API small. Clients can pass precomputed features. I propose these params: model, max_candidates (client request upper bound <= server cap), include_raw_scores (bool), return_rank (bool, default true), stable_tiebreaker="id".
Alicia (platform): Good. We also need to decide on score scaling: Min/Max normalization or logistic?
Priya (eng-ml): Implementation detail: we can min-max per-batch which is unstable across batches. Better to apply a sigmoid on logits to get (0,1) but that also depends on logit scale. Maybe document that normalized score is sigmoid(raw_score) by default for ranking models that output logits.
Ben (api): Sigmoid default is fine but call it out. Also include field "score_type": "sigmoid" or "raw" in response metadata so clients know.
Zoe (product): For rollout UX: can we route 1% of rerank traffic to a new ranking model and show score distribution + downstream CTR/metric in console?
Marco (console): Yes — add rollout knob in Console routes: rerank.model override with canary percentage. Telemetry pipeline must stream score_histogram, candidate_count, avg_rank_position for tracked keys.
Priya (eng-ml): Also need to be careful about exposing raw_score because it can leak model internals. Make include_raw_scores restricted to enterprise tenants or require a flag in tenant settings.
Alicia (platform): Good call. Let's default include_raw_scores=false and make it an account-level opt-in if needed.
Ben (api): Sample response format draft:
```json
{
  "request_id": "r_12345",
  "model": "rerank-2024-01",
  "score_type": "sigmoid",
  "items": [
    {"candidate_id": "c_7", "rank": 1, "score": 0.982},
    {"candidate_id": "c_2", "rank": 2, "score": 0.870}
  ],
  "meta": {"candidate_count": 12, "normalization": "sigmoid"}
}
```
Priya (eng-ml): Looks good. For include_raw_scores: add "raw_score" inside each item when requested.
Marco (console): For dashboards we should ingest per-request summary: model, model_version, candidate_count, max_score, mean_score, p50_score, p95_latency_ms. Also tag rollout_variant.
Ben (api): Telemetry names: rerank.requests, rerank.candidate_count, rerank.latency_ms, rerank.score.max, rerank.score.mean. We'll emit stats with model and tenant tags.
Alicia (platform): Edge cases: empty candidates list -> return 200 with items: [] and reason field maybe. Also if client requests > server cap -> return 400 with useful error and header X-Allowed-Max-Candidates.
Priya (eng-ml): Also think about scoring ties when scores equal to machine precision — stable sort + return deterministic rank is required.
Zoe (product): Any thought on default model selection? If model param omitted, pick a default reranker per tenant (configurable).
Alicia (platform): Yes, configure default_rerank_model at tenant level. If not present, use global default. We'll list it in API docs.
Ben (api): Backwards compatibility: current experimental /search rerank used a different response. We'll version the endpoint as /v2/rerank and keep old one for a quarter.
Priya (eng-ml): Perf note: support streaming candidate evaluation? probably not; rerank needs full candidate set. But we can support partial early-stop when top K found? complicated. Skip for now.
Marco (console): For rollout UX: add small traffic visualizer in Console: live qps, canary percent, and score shift delta vs baseline.
Alicia (platform): OK action items: Ben send api schema PR with these fields; Priya include normalization and privacy notes; Marco add telemetry spec and dashboard widgets; Zoe add product notes about tenant defaults and rollout UX. I'll draft the PR by EOD. :thumbsup:
Ben (api): On it.
Priya (eng-ml): I'll put a short section in the reranker README about what "score" means and include examples for different model families.
Marco (console): I'll stub dashboard panels and wire the tags.
rerank-bot: Deploy job queued for canary routing config change (job id dj-7782) :robot_face:
Alicia (platform): Thanks all. We'll loop back after the PR review.
